x-fc-pending.title: Pending of the spec
x-fc-pending.description: Fields and shapes the API in production has (see `sources`, each one with the release it was read in) where the spec in spec/funnelchat.json, the one the developer portal publishes, describes an operation or an event otherwise than production answers, or only by an example. scripts/generate.mjs applies them to the spec before generating the types, only while the spec still lacks them or still says what a `while` / `x-fc-replace-while` names: when a new spec brings them, generation uses the spec and lists the entries of this file that can be deleted. The layer corrects what the spec publishes and never adds to it: an operation or an event the spec does not publish is not typed.

rules.operationPatches: A patch adds properties to the body, or `parameters`, to a snapshot operation. With `while`, only while that operation matches it; without `while`, each one only while the operation lacks it.
rules.webhooks: An event replaces the one the spec publishes while that one matches `x-fc-replace-while`. An event the spec does not publish is not added.
rules.responsePatches: A patch replaces the responses of a snapshot operation (every 2xx, and the other codes it brings) only while that operation matches `while`.
rules.components.schemas: The schemas of this layer start with `Pending` so they never clash with the snapshot's.
rules.schemaPatches: A patch adds properties to a snapshot schema, each one only while the schema lacks it.
rules.while: In `while` and `x-fc-replace-while`, a key is a property of the operation (or of the event's `post`), or, when it starts with `/`, a JSON Pointer into it (RFC 6901): the entry applies only while that exact place still holds that value.

sources.accounts-webhooks: accounts v1.4.24 (in production on 22-10-2026): the webhook subscription routes open to API keys, their bodies and answers, the Notifications (webhooks) permissions and the events of each area. Read again in accounts v1.5.97 (in production on 04-11-2026): the same routes, bodies and answers; since then a subscription belongs to the workspace of the key that creates it, and the cap of 50 counts per workspace. `PUT webhooks/{id}` answers the subscription, which the spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) types as `{type: object}`.
sources.conversations-send: conversations v1.19.21 (in production on 05-11-2026; first read in v1.19.7): every single send of a key (text, send-message, template, form) answers `200 {message}` with the message it registered, never `null`. The spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) documents that `message` as nullable.
sources.conversations-status: conversations v1.19.21 (in production on 05-11-2026; first read in v1.19.7): the `data` of message.status_changed. The spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) shows it only by an example (`schema: {type: object}`): `status` as any string and `client_reference` never null.
sources.conversations-forms: conversations v1.18.10 (in production on 22-10-2026): WhatsApp forms, their routes and answers, and the `data` of whatsapp_form.completed. Read again in conversations v1.19.7 (in production on 04-11-2026): the same `data`; the send route also checks that the contact is of the key's workspace. The spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) shows whatsapp_form.completed only by an example: every answer a string and no field null.
sources.communities-events: communities v2.34.52 (in production on 22-10-2026): the `data` of the group events, relayed by the event catalog of accounts v1.4.24. Read again in the releases in production on 04-11-2026 (accounts v1.5.97, conversations v1.19.7, communities v2.35.5): group_participant.joined and .left as communities v2.35.5 sends them (`campaign` null for a group without a campaign), and group_action.completed as accounts v1.5.97 relays it. communities v2.35.28 (in production on 11-11-2026): group.message_received and group.reaction_added carry `message.uid`, although the example of the spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) says `message.id`.
sources.accounts-number-signup: accounts v1.5.97 (in production on 04-11-2026; first in v1.4.38): creating numbers and connect links, the `connection` and `external_reference` of a number, and the connect page (the QR every 5 seconds, 10 minutes to scan it from the page; the official sign-up by link answers `503 meta_connect_disabled` in production). The seven device.* events, all active: the same `device` block in all of them, `connect_link_id` and `reason`. The spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) shows them only by an example.
sources.conversations-received: conversations v1.19.21 (in production on 05-11-2026; first read in v1.19.7): the `data` of message.received: `text` and `media` null when absent, phones as `+` and digits or null, `device_id` last. The spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) types it as its example shows: `text` and the phones never null, `media` unknown.
sources.conversations-templates: conversations v1.19.21 (in production on 05-11-2026; first read in v1.19.7): `GET templates` answers a page of templates, with the quality counts. The spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) types its items as `{type: object}`.
sources.accounts-qr: accounts v1.5.97 (in production on 04-11-2026): `GET devices/{device}/qr` answers `{data: {connected, qr_code, expires_in}}`. The spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) infers a union of that body, the inner object in three forms and a bare string.
sources.communities-group-action: communities v2.35.5 (in production on 04-11-2026): `GET groups/actions/{action}` answers `{data: <one action>}`. The spec the portal publishes (portal v0.6.13) types `data` as an array.

PendingDeviceConnection.description: `qr`: connected by scanning a QR code (not official). `coexistence`: WhatsApp Cloud API together with the WhatsApp Business app. `dedicated`: WhatsApp Cloud API only. `null` when it cannot be told yet.

PendingExternalReference.description: Your own reference for the number (for example the id of your customer). Free text, not unique.

identity.description: The phone in digits, without `+`, or a `…@lid`.

qr_code.description: A PNG image as a data URI, or `null` when the number is already connected.

expires_in.description: Seconds after which to ask for it again: 5 with a QR, 3 while the session starts, 0 once connected. WhatsApp changes the code every few seconds and an old one no longer links: show the latest one and have it scanned right away; do not store or forward a QR.

type.description: `send_message` for a message to the group.

result.description: `{}` while it is open. Sending: `{message: {uid}}`, the id of the message in WhatsApp. Other actions: `{participants: [...]}`, `{group, invite_link}` or `{invite_link}`.

200.description: The message was registered (`status: queued`, or `failed` with `not_queued`) and goes out from the queue.
The message was registered (`status: queued`, or `failed` with `not_queued`) and goes out from the queue.
The message was registered (`status: queued`, or `failed` with `not_queued`) and goes out from the queue.
The message was registered (`status: queued`, or `failed` with `not_queued`) and goes out from the queue.
The QR to show, or `connected: true` once it was scanned.

post.description: One of the numbers of the account got connected: by scanning the QR code, by finishing the sign-up of a WhatsApp Cloud number, or through a connect link.

connect_link_id.description: The connect link of this connection, or `null` when it did not come from a link.

post.description: One of the numbers of the account disconnected and can no longer send or receive: a QR session that closed or was protected from a shadow ban, an official number that failed its re-registration, or one disconnected from the panel.

connect_link_id.description: The connect link that last connected the number, or `null`.

post.description: A charge of the subscription could not be processed (Stripe subscriptions only).
The next charge of the subscription is coming up (Stripe subscriptions only).
The dormant-account period is about to end.
An action on a group of a campaign failed.

uuid.description: `null` for the actions of a campaign.

post.description: Someone wrote in a group of one of your numbers. Not emitted for the messages of your own numbers.
Someone reacted to a message of a group.
Someone asked to join a group that requires approval.
Someone withdrew their request to join a group.
A number of the account was deleted (from the panel, the API, or because a connect link expired without connecting it): its slot of the plan is free again.

connect_link_id.description: The connect link that last connected the number, or `null`.

post.description: The health of an official number changed (what Meta lets it do). Emitted only when the overall state changes.

connect_link_id.description: The connect link that last connected the number, or `null`.

post.description: The quality Meta gives an official number changed (`GREEN`, `YELLOW` or `RED`, as Meta sends them). If it drops, slow down the sends of that number before Meta limits it. Once per change; not when Meta has no quality data.

connect_link_id.description: The connect link that last connected the number, or `null`.

post.description: The messaging limit Meta gives an official number changed: how many different people it can start a conversation with per day (`TIER_250`, `TIER_1K`, `TIER_2K`, `TIER_10K`, `TIER_100K` or `TIER_UNLIMITED`). Meta sets it per business: one notice per number of the account that changed.

connect_link_id.description: The connect link that last connected the number, or `null`.

post.description: Meta approved or rejected the display name of an official number.

rejection_reason.description: Meta's reason in a rejection, or `null`.

connect_link_id.description: The connect link that last connected the number, or `null`.

post.description: A group action asked through the API finished, such as a message to a group. `action.uuid` is the `action_id` it returned; sending, `result.message.uid` is the id of the message in WhatsApp.

result.description: Sending: `message.uid`; with phones: `participants`; creating or renewing the link: `invite_link`; the rest, empty.

post.description: A person joined one of the account's groups.

campaign.description: `null` when the group is not of a campaign.

identity.description: The phone, or a `…@lid` when WhatsApp does not show it.

post.description: A person left one of the account's groups.

campaign.description: `null` when the group is not of a campaign.

identity.description: The phone, or a `…@lid` when WhatsApp does not show it.

post.description: A contact wrote to one of the WhatsApp numbers of the account.

id.description: The id of the message in the history of the contact.

text.description: `null` when the message has no text (a file without caption, say).

phone.description: `+` and digits, or `null` when the contact has no phone (a `@lid`, say).
The phone of your number that received it, `+` and digits.

device_id.description: The number of your account that received the message: the same `device_id` you send to reply through it. `null` when the message has no number.

post.description: The delivery status of a message you sent with the API changed. One notice per transition, never one that goes back; `queued` is not reported. It must be asked for explicitly in `events`.

message_id.description: The `id` of the message in the history of the contact.

device_id.description: The number of your account that sent the message.

error.description: Only when `status` is `failed`. Why it failed. When Funnelchat stopped it, `code` is `null` and `reason` says why; when it failed in WhatsApp, `code` and `title` are the provider's and `reason` is `null`.

client_reference.description: The `client_reference` you sent with the message, or `null`.

post.description: A contact completed a form you sent them.
